title: Folklorism drying up as a source for art
summary: Folk and regional cultures no longer feed art.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: as any field that I can think of.
I think any art will do it, but it effects art quicker than it does anything else. I think that's one of the reasons for the malaise in the whole artistic scene.
For so long, for a hundred fifty, two hundred years, they used folklorism as a basis and suddenly what was life giving about folklorism, that kind of folklorism, no longer is so.
(Side A of Tape 3 ended at this point. Transcript will continue with Side B.)

--it suddenly dried up and although there may be a new folkloreism developing, I'm almost convinced that there is, but it will be of a different type. It won't be anything that we've known before, we can't go to the old national cultures, regional cultures and get the stimulus that we did in another time. That was all from the age of the explorers.
Of those cultures that have in effect heard things that have developed since then and they're kind of simulated, there is very little that is "pure."
Nothing is pure anymore; if it ever was. It's one world that quickly, and I think too quickly, for the human mind to adjust to it.
